rows.description: A toddler shows surprise with wide eyes and a gasp, and confusion with frowning or looking to a caregiver. Adults provide reassurance and a short explanation to help make sense of novelty.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler nods, shakes the head and says no, often for the sense of control rather than true opposition. Adults offer limited choices to honour the need for autonomy.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler reaches, points or says more to request food, help or a toy. The request may also carry a need for comfort, so adults name it, such as you want up.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler responds to a sharp no, a raised voice or a gasp as a sign of danger. Simple short words and physical safety matter more than long explanations at this age.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Refusing with no and pulling away [Expressing]
rows.description: A toddler refuses by saying no, turning away or pushing an object or hand away. Adults respect small refusals about touch and food where safe, and this teaches that the body belongs to the child.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler offers a toy or a bite of food to show sharing and social interest. It is often a spontaneous gesture, and a warm response reinforces kindness without forcing it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler pats a crying friend or brings a toy to comfort, showing early care. It is an emerging sign of empathy that adults reinforce with warm notice.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: affection, sadness, empathy

rows.description: A toddler shows love and closeness by cuddling, reaching to be held and seeking a familiar caregiver. The child also has the right to refuse a hug or kiss from relatives, and adults respect that.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler hands over a toy, hugs, or says a prompted "thank you" after a gift. The gesture often follows adult modelling and may carry real pleasure before it carries a grasp of gratitude.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler calms to a slow, low voice, rocking and gentle touch even before understanding words. Tone and closeness carry the reassurance; sudden or tense handling can undo it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
